title: POST https://api.bistudio.com/user/api/v2.0/auth/login
$comment: The second half of the client's login, reached by probing rather than by watching a game. The body's requirement is exactly one field: an empty body answers `<body> should have required property 'client_id'`, and a well-shaped client_id is accepted without complaint, so nothing else is required. That id must match `^\$[A-Za-z0-9]{31}$` - the same value the build sends as the x-client-id header on every other call. With a valid-shaped id the answer becomes 401 Unauthorized, so the call is gated on an authenticated session that this schema cannot describe: it is what the flow at accounts.bistudio.com (the config's URI_AccountApi) hands the client. The binary's field list for this operation, read next to the path in the executable, is client_id, two_factor_token, access_token, and its classes are UserApiDirectAuth / UserApiRequestDirectAuth / UserApiResponseDirectAuth / UserApiErrorResponseDirectAuth; the response fields were never seen. Nothing here can be done with a server token - the whole point of section 5 of docs/en/ArmaReforger_BackendAPI_EN.md.

client_id.description: The client application's id, `$` plus 31 alphanumerics. In every captured build it is the same string that travels as the x-client-id header, so the login authenticates the application by the credential it already carries. A wrong-but-well-shaped id is not distinguished from a right one in the probes: both answer 401.

two_factor_token.description: Named by the binary for this call, and the error vocabulary has `authService.missing2FA` and `authService.invalid2FA` beside `authService.invalidCredentials`, so accounts with a second factor are handled here rather than in the browser step.

access_token.description: Named by the binary for this call. What it carries - a code from the account flow or a platform ticket - was not established; no request with one was ever seen.

unauthorized.description: What the service answers to a well-formed body without a session: 401, message Unauthorized, desc UNAUTHORIZED, and no api_code at all.

uid.description: Per-request id; a number here, unlike the game API's UUID.
